minutes.headline: Committee voted to swap FY26 capital projects for funds to finish a grant-funded mini-split project
minutes.summary: An emergency school committee meeting was called to decide whether to amend the FY26 capital plan, pulling several school capital projects (playground and driveway design studies, safety window film, and a Turkey Hill hot water tank replacement, among others) and replacing them with funding to complete phase two of the mini-split installation at the primary school, in order to use a Green Communities grant before it expires and free the town to apply for further grants. After extended discussion about the funding math, the abruptness of the request, and tradeoffs against deferred safety projects, the committee voted by roll call to endorse the town manager's and superintendent's plan to modify the capital plan request.

votes.motion: Endorse the town manager and superintendent's plan to modify the FY26 capital plan request (removing certain school capital projects and substituting funding to complete mini-split phase two at the primary school) and send that request back to the town manager.
votes.outcome: passed (roll call: Scholenrini yes, Pazilki yes, Beardmore yes, chair yes)
passed (roll call: Scullen yes, Pazowski yes, Beardmore yes, chair yes)

decisions.decision: Projects removed from the FY26 capital plan for this purpose (playground design study, driveway design study, safety window film, Turkey Hill hot water tank, security camera server) would be brought back for consideration in the FY27 ten-year capital plan.

The Friday working group of superintendent, Dr. Gillson, the finance committee chair, the select board chair, and the school committee chair will continue meeting routinely on capital/grant coordination.
This vote will be placed on a future non-emergency meeting agenda as a regular item to reconfirm it, ahead of informing Green Communities and the select board.

what_happened.line: The committee voted by roll call to endorse a plan pulling several FY26 school capital projects to fund finishing a grant-funded mini-split project.
Projects removed to free that funding -- playground and driveway design studies, safety window film, a hot water tank replacement -- return for FY27 capital plan consideration.
Members identified a funding shortfall after adding the grant and a utility incentive, and discussed covering it from free cash.
The vote will be placed on a future non-emergency meeting agenda for reconfirmation before the town notifies the grant program and the select board.

why_it_matters: This swaps out school maintenance and safety-related capital items this year in favor of a grant deadline, so residents may not see those projects funded until FY27.
The discussed shortfall would draw on free cash, a town-wide reserve, giving this decision a reach beyond the school budget alone.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the single substantive fact — the committee endorsed the amended FY26 capital plan sending mini-split funding back to the town manager, and it passed — but the official minutes are a one-paragraph summary that omits nearly every figure, sub-decision, and transfer our minutes captured from the recording, while adding a motion-maker/seconder and a public-comment line ours lack.
